subject: design-technology
title: Glass Fibre and Smart Materials
welcome_lead: GFRP boats and smart materials that respond to environment.
meta_desc: A-Level D&T: GFRP composites and smart materials.
final_note: Materials that change with their environment.

concepts.def: Material whose property changes in response to a stimulus.
Alloy (e.g. Nitinol) that returns to a 'remembered' shape on heating.
Material producing voltage when mechanically stressed.
Material changing colour with applied voltage (smart glazing).

walkthroughs.body_html: GFRP uses glass fibres in polyester or epoxy resin. Cheaper and less stiff than CFRP, it dominates boat hulls, wind-turbine blades and water tanks. Hand lay-up and resin infusion are common processes.
Nitinol (nickel-titanium SMA) is used in stents and spectacle frames. Piezoelectric ceramics (PZT) drive ultrasound transducers and inkjet print heads.
Thermochromic dyes shift colour with temperature (kettles, baby spoons). Electrochromic glazing darkens under voltage (Boeing 787 windows).
